currentRepair.sourceTitle: throws a descriptive error when rendered outside <Slider.Root>
currentRepair.evidence: Required SliderRootContext hook now throws exact upstream Base UI message. Review file16/16 Chromium; full jsdom passes. Supersedes all historical missing-context red findings below, not the two unresolved prehydration geometry cases or event-target adaptation.

method: Manual body comparison of every family test/spec and utility fixture. A row's sourceFile, lane, conditions and targetFile inherit its containing section. Titles alone do not establish a match. Multiple source rows can map to one target only when the listed interactions and assertions survive. Parameter tables are explicit concrete invocations, not regex/title inference.
status: all family files manually reviewed; coverage additions verified; source error-message regression remains red and two browser SSR geometry cases remain gaps
frameworkAdaptations: Native input replaces React synthetic change; accepted value is the callback argument. Native event.target remains the input, not the React cloned {name,value} object. The cloned event target source assertion is an explicit API adaptation concern, not matched.

Owned factories and renderProps live proxies replace React rerender/useState/act. Await user interactions and live patches; use existing synchronous-observation flush only where already present. New packet helpers yield one microtask after a dispatched event, not a blanket drain.

Solid class and native render callback/ref composition replace className/element-clone/ref-object machinery. Browser-only source predicates remain browser requirements even when additional jsdom regression evidence exists.

Source Touch helpers construct changedTouches with document.body as Touch.target; target native packet helper retains that target and event origin. Source rect defaults are 100x10; browser packet root fixture uses 100x100 but horizontal mapping remains width=100, vertical height=100. Thumb layout suites use source 100/1000px geometry explicitly.
